newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria says U.S. proposed Africa force targets it.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria says U.S. proposed Africa force targets it.

text.p: The military authorities in Lagos said on Tuesday that a United States proposal to set up an African crisis response force was aimed at underming Nigeria's leading role in peace-keeping on the continent.
Nigerian troops form the bulk of an African peace-keeping force in Liberia, Africa's oldest republic set by freed American slaves which has been in crisis since 1989.

The state news agency said acting defence ministry spokesman Colonel Godwin Ugbo told reporters in Lagos that Nigeria was not bothered by the proposal because it had failed to receive the full support of the Organisation of African Unity (OAU).
"Any decision taken without the support of the OAU is obviously not in the interest of Africa," he said.
Nigeria-U.S. relations are at their worst over alleged human rights abuses by Nigeria's military government and the slow pace of restoring democracy in the country.
African leaders including President Nelson Mandela of South Africa have expressed caution about the U.S. proposal to set a 10,000-strong African Crisis Reaction Force.
Mandela told U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher at the weekend that the project should not be seen as coming from one country, but rather through a body such as the United Nations.
